items.content_text:
On Thursday, July 30, 2026, Sheriff Austin Garrett and the Hamilton County Sheriff’s Office Corrections Services hosted a Corrections Academy Graduation Ceremony for Class 26-02, recognizing the successful completion of training by six new corrections deputies.
 Graduates of Class 26-02 completed 292 hours of comprehensive training in general corrections operations, legal studies, firearms proficiency, physical fitness and endurance, and self-defense tactics, exceeding the minimum training requirements established by the Tennessee Corrections Institute (TCI).
 During the ceremony, Hamilton County Sessions Court Judge Tori Smith administered the oath of office to the graduates. Corrections Deputy Piersen Sukienski was selected by his peers to serve as Class Leader, while Deputy Daniel Darby received the Top Shot award, and Deputy Michelle Imre received the Academic Award.
 The graduates of Corrections Academy Class 26-02 are:
 Michelle Imre
 Darian Simonsen
 Benjamin Cates
 Piersen Sukienik
 Daniel Darby
 Ryan White
 The Hamilton County Sheriff’s Office congratulates these new Corrections Deputies and wishes them success as they begin their careers serving in the Hamilton County Jail & Detention Center.

Congratulations! ArtsBuild Announces 2026–2027 Artists Work Grant Recipients
 ArtsBuild has awarded $135,000 through its 2026–2027 Artists Work grant program, supporting 30 local artists and artist teams who will create free and low-cost arts experiences throughout Hamilton County.
 Artists Work grants of up to $5,000 support projects that strengthen neighborhoods, expand access to the arts, and contribute to the local creative economy.
 “ArtsBuild understands that art should be accessible to everyone, everywhere,” said Melissa Astin, Director of Grants and Community Engagement. “These artists will activate public spaces with projects that reflect Hamilton County’s unique culture and communities.”
 Recipients: Liza Blair; Jake Brown & Abby Lusk; Jon Brumit; Courtenay Cholovich (Lookout Comedy); LeBron Clay (Ashe Core Youth Foundation); Brandi Donan; Jerigray Eduave; Aaron Ellison "Coach Cherokee"; Matt Eslinger; Jessi Faircloth (collectively/here); Regina Gee; Chase Guajardo; Grace Haley; Julius Johnson; N'nako Kande'; Ryan Laskowski (Scenic City Shakespeare); Jered Martin, Kota Riemer & Tessa Voccola; Melissa Meade; Kevin McCurdy (Misfit Metal); Lucius Nelson; Kashun Parks, Holly Morse-Ellington & Jason Tinney (Next Exit Productions); Jaime Peterson; Dominique Pruitt; Shateria Smith (brown girls can); Jason Tinney; Alex Volz; Josh Wheeler; Tron Wilder (Southern Adventist University); Sarah Yvonne (Ballet Esprit); Andrea Zoppo.
 Projects include photography, theater, dance, music, public art, film, comedy, wearable art, creative arts therapy, storytelling, animation, oral history, ceramics, puppetry, and community festivals, with public events taking place across Hamilton County through early 2027.
 Learn more about upcoming grant-funded events by subscribing to ArtsWire at artsbuild.com. Artists and community members are also invited to attend ArtsBuild's monthly open house; dates are available at artsbuild.com/events.
 The Artists Work Grant program is supported by Mark Making, The Robert Finley Stone Foundation, The Lyndhurst Foundation, The Benwood Foundation, and individual ArtsBuild donors.

Like many others, I started college right after high school. At the time, I was doing what I thought I was “supposed” to do, but deep down I didn’t have a clear sense of purpose. Soon after, my parents went through a difficult divorce that deeply affected me. I lost focus, stopped attending classes, and eventually stepped away from college completely.
 Years passed, but I always knew I wanted a career where I could help others. In 2023, I decided to take the leap and return to college with a new mindset—and a new goal: to become a registered nurse. This time, I was fully committed and ready to do whatever it took to achieve my dream. 
 TN Reconnect made my return possible. Without it, the financial burden might have stopped me again. But with their support, I was able to focus on my education without the weight of tuition costs holding me back. I now have the clarity, drive, and resources to succeed, and I am proud to say I am pursuing a future in nursing with everything I’ve got.
 If you’re considering going back to school later in life, I want you to know it’s never too late. TN Reconnect has truly changed my life, and I will always be thankful for the opportunity it has given me to chase my dream of becoming a nurse.

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
 July 30th, 2026
 Hamilton County Health & Social Services Encourages Families to Get Back-to-School Vaccines Before the New School Year.
 HAMILTON COUNTY, TN— As students prepare to return to school, the Hamilton County Health and Social Services Division is urging parents and guardians to ensure their children receive all required and recommended school immunizations. These vaccinations will help ensure a healthy start to the school year. The Health Department encourages parents and guardians to avoid last-minute rushes and long wait times by planning ahead and getting their children vaccinated early. No appointment is necessary at the 3rd Street or Birchwood Health Department clinics.
 Vaccinations are one of the most effective ways to protect children, families, and the community from preventable and potentially life-threatening diseases. By getting immunizations before the school year begins, students can meet Tennessee's school requirements while also helping to reduce the spread of vaccine-preventable illnesses in classrooms. 
 The Hamilton County Health & Social Services Division offers school-required and recommended vaccines, including:
 • DTaP/Tdap (Diphtheria, Tetanus, and Pertussis)
 • Polio (IPV)
 • Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR)
 • Varicella (Chickenpox)
 • Hepatitis A & B
 • Meningococcal 
 • Human Papillomavirus (HPV) (recommended)
 The Pediatric Clinic is located inside the Travel and Adult Immunizations Clinic, on the first floor of the west side wing of the Health Department. 
 Immunization records are available:

Swimming is a fantastic way to stay active and enjoy the summer!
 Before heading to the pool or splash pad, remember to follow these important steps to protect yourself and others:
 - Shower before entering the water.
 - Cover any open wounds with a waterproof bandage.
 - Avoid swallowing pool water.
 - Use a well-fitting, Coast Guard-approved life jacket to help you float; do not rely on air-filled toys like water wings.
 - Take regular bathroom breaks and check young children's diapers every hour.
 - Do not swim if you have diarrhea.
 By following these guidelines, you can help ensure a safe and enjoyable swimming experience for everyone!
 For more information on healthy swimming practices, visit [CDC Healthy Swimming] (https://www.cdc.gov/healthy-swimming/prevention/index.html).

Labour markets are changing fast, widening the gap between the skills employers’ need and those people have. 
 An OECD report shows how skills-first approaches – focusing on what people can do, not just their qualifications – can help improve hiring, boost productivity and widen access to opportunities.
 It explores the importance of a shared understanding of the skills needed for each occupation, micro-credentials, and better recognition of prior learning, and provides insights on how countries and firms are adopting these practices.
 Placing greater emphasis on skills can support more resilient, inclusive and dynamic economies.
 Read the report: https://brnw.ch/21x4xSt

items.content_text:
✈️ There’s still time to help shape the future of the Collegedale Municipal Airport!
 The City of Collegedale is still accepting Letters of Interest from individuals who would like to serve on the new advisory Airport Board.
 The five-member board will provide recommendations to the City Commission regarding the operation and use of the airport. Three members must live within Collegedale city limits, while two may live outside the city.
 📅 Deadline: Friday, August 21, at 12 noon
 📧 Email: kwheeler@collegedaletn.gov
 📍 Letters may also be delivered to Collegedale City Hall.
 See the original post for the complete application requirements. Your experience and perspective could make a meaningful difference in our community!
The City of Collegedale has created an advisory Airport Board, and the City is soliciting Letters of Interest from candidates who would like to serve on that board. 
 The Airport Board is tasked by the Collegedale City Commission with recommending such rules and regulations concerning the operation and use of the Collegedale Municipal Airport to the Collegedale City commission for consideration and formal adoption as the City Commission may deem necessary and appropriate. Such rules shall be recommended as may be consistent with the public interest and the public health, safety and general welfare of the airport and the Collegedale community.  The Collegedale Tennessee Airport Board will be advisory in capacity to the City Commission.
 City residency is not required for all appointments.  The Board consists of five (5) individuals.  The Board makeup must consist of three (3) citizens whose primary residence is within the City Limits of the City of Collegedale, and two (2) citizens may be appointed that live outside the city limits of the City of Collegedale. Residents appointed to the Airport Board shall serve for a three-year term.  Non-Residents shall serve for an initial one-year term, and future reappointments will be for two-year terms.  
 To be considered for appointment to the Airport Board, please submit a Letter of Interest that provides the following: 
 1. Your primary residential address and indicate whether it is located inside or outside the city limits of the City of Collegedale. 
 2. A brief statement about why you are interested in serving on Airport Board. 
 3. Any information about yourself, your qualifications and experiences that you believe would be beneficial for appointment to the Airport Advisory Board. A resume’ would be acceptable for this information. 
 Interested parties may submit their Letter of Interest in person or as an attachment to an email no later than 12 Noon, on Friday August 21st.  
 To submit your Letter of Interest in person please submit it at the Collegedale City Hall no later than 12 Noon, Friday August 21st: 
 Collegedale City Hall 4910 Swinyar Drive Collegedale, TN 37315-1880 
 To submit your Letter of Interest as an attachment to an email, please send it to kwheeler@collegedaletn.gov no later than 12 Noon Friday August 21st.

 Hamilton County, TN – Recently, the HCSO’s Strategic Enforcement Unit (SEU) more than doubled the number of arrests and citations compared to last year’s summer initiative.
 The SEU is made up of eight HCSO deputies from the patrol and school resource deputy units. The HCSO Crime Analysis Unit investigations fuel this eight-week data-driven initiative, focusing on proactive law enforcement, promoting traffic safety, suppressing violent crime, apprehending fugitives, and interdicting narcotics, while also offering quick-response municipal support for priority calls.
 Our personnel conducted numerous specialized enforcements, including DUI enforcement, targeted narcotics interdiction, registered sex offender warrant operations, and more.

 • 703 Traffic Stops
 • 381 Traffic Citations 
 • 78 Citations in Lieu of Arrest
 • 67 Arrests 
 • 36 Field Interviews 
 • 65 Countywide Priority Calls for Service
 • 10 Vehicle Pursuits
 Recovered the following:
 • 15 Firearms 
 • 32 Drug Seizures
 The variety of calls for service spread across many high-priority incidents, including shootings, stabbings, armed robberies, domestic violence, barricaded subjects, assaults, multi-agency warrant services, and more.

items.content_text:
Colorectal cancer remains one of the top three causes of cancer in OECD countries - but it is also one of the most preventable.  
 Earlier detection and improved treatment mean that deaths are falling, but there is still much to be done to improve prognosis. 
 ➡️Fewer than half (48%) of eligible people were screened in 2023, and participation varies eight-fold across OECD countries. 
 ➡️People with lower education levels have colorectal cancer screening rates that are 9 percentage points lower on average than those with higher education across OECD countries 
 ➡️Colorectal cancer is still being caught too late – with many patients arriving at the emergency department once the disease has already become severe.  
 Learn what governments can do to improve the outlook for colorectal cancer here: https://brnw.ch/21x4wMT

What does tourism investment really look like?

It isn't always a new attraction or a postcard-worthy destination. Sometimes, it's restoring access to the places that make Southeast Tennessee special.

The Southeast Tennessee Tourism Association (SETTA), a program at SETD, partners with local communities to support projects that strengthen tourism, expand outdoor recreation, and improve quality of life across our region through tourism enhancement. 

These before-and-after photos showcase the transformation of the Hiwassee River Blueway Access Point at Cherokee Crossing in Calhoun through a Tourism Enhancement Grant that was administered by SETTA. What was once an underutilized river access point is now a welcoming destination for kayaking, fishing, picnics, and enjoying one of Southeast Tennessee's greatest assets — nature!  

This project is a reminder that tourism isn't just about attracting visitors — it's about investing in the infrastructure that supports rural communities, fuels local economies, and creates places people are proud to call home.

items.content_text:
Collegedale TimberFest Brings Chainsaw Art and Family Fun 
 COLLEGEDALE, TN (07/29/2026) - A brand-new community tradition is coming to the greater Collegedale and Ooltewah area this summer. Collegedale TimberFest will make its debut August 21–23, 2026, at The Commons, 4750 Swinyar Drive in Ooltewah, bringing together talented chainsaw artists, local artisans, food vendors, and family-friendly activities for an exciting three-day festival.
 The weekend celebrates the remarkable art of chainsaw carving, where skilled craftsmen transform massive logs into beautiful sculptures before spectators' eyes. Throughout the festival, visitors will have the opportunity to watch each piece evolve from raw timber into a finished work of art.
 Sawdust begins to fly on Friday, August 21, as artists arrive to set up their carving areas and prepare for the competition. An optional public carving session from 4 p.m. to 7 p.m. offers an early look at the creative process. Chainsaw carving artist, Carole Chubbuck says that they “are excited and looking forward to entertaining the community with our artistry, taking ordinary logs and turning them into beautiful sculptures before your eyes.”
 The main festival takes place on Saturday, August 22, with live carving demonstrations from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. One of the day's featured attractions is the Quick Carve Competition from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m., where artists race against the clock to create a sculpture in just one hour. These unique pieces will then be placed in a silent auction, which begins at 2 p.m. on Saturday and concludes at noon on Sunday.
 Visitors can also enjoy an artisan vendor market and food trucks from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., along with a Kids Corner and other activities designed to entertain the entire family. Co-organizers, Lumberjack Tree Services’ LumberJulie said “It will be awesome to see people experience the tree and lumber industry in a whole new way! Not only will this festival be fun and entertaining, but we also hope it will be educational and inspiring to the community.”
 On Sunday, August 23, carving continues from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., followed by the Judging and Awards Ceremony from 2 p.m. to 3 p.m. The completed sculptures will then be available for
 purchase during the festival's sculpture sale and auction, giving attendees the opportunity to take home a one-of-a-kind work of art.
 More than a showcase of exceptional talent, Collegedale TimberFest is designed to bring the community together while supporting local artists, businesses, and craftsmen. Co-organizers, Collegedale Parks & Recreation’s Supervisor, Christina Clark says she hopes the inaugural event will become a signature annual tradition that draws visitors from across the region.
 Whether you're interested in watching talented chainsaw artists at work, shopping handcrafted goods, enjoying great local food, or spending a fun weekend with family and friends, Collegedale TimberFest promises something for everyone.
 Mark your calendar for August 21–23 and be part of the very first Collegedale TimberFest—where creativity, community, and craftsmanship come together.

items.content_text:
Tuesday, July 28, 2026
 TSMA RESPONSE TONIGHT ON MASSIVE HOUSE FIRE. 
 This evening, a seventy year old grandmother rescues five children ranging from 2 infant twins, 7 YO and (2) 9 YO’s from a massive house fire on Walden’s Ridge. At 5:30 pm, a 911 call was made reporting a garage fire located at 515 Gentlemen Ridge in Brow Estates subdivision. Walden’s Ridge Emergency Service (WRES) responded and arrived on the scene reporting heavy smoke and fire in the garage. Firefighters worked quickly to establish water supply. WRES requested a large mutual aid response for additional manpower and apparatus. Signal Mountain Fire Department, Chattanooga Fire Department, Dallas Bay VFD, Lone Oak VFD, Red Bank Fire Department and Mutual Aid Chief 6 Mike Williams, and Chattanooga-Hamilton County Rescue responded to the fire scene. 
 Firefighters worked quickly to get the garage fire under control. However, fire entered the attic and spread quickly throughout the entire roofline. By 6:10 pm, fire officials reported the 13,000 square foot home was fully involved and firefighters were starting  a defensive attack to contain the fire.  Damages are extensive. No injuries were reported but HCEMS was on the scene checking firefighters for potential heat exhaustion. The cause of the fire will be under investigation by the Hamilton County Sheriffs Office. Family will be staying with neighbors.

Tomorrow afternoon will be a huge moment for me. I’ll lead one of two presentations / walking tours from the Chattanooga Convention Center to the historic Chattanooga Choo Choo as part of the NMRA 2026 Scenic City Express - Chattanooga Convention. To be a guest presenter is already an honor, and to speak in front of so many incredibly talented people will be even more so.
 During the presentation and walking tour, I’ll have one of my greatest possessions on my person… the copy of my book “Chattanooga’s Terminal Station” given to my grandparents.  This was the very first copy of my book I signed.
 My first model train was a Lionel Trains set, opened on a Christmas morning at my grandparents house.  And now I find myself speaking in front of the NMRA - National Model Railroad Association. If this isn’t a story about how a model train can change a life… 
 Grandma and Grandpa, I will be forever grateful to ya’ll for the little nudge that caused an avalanche of inspiration.  I miss you both, I love you both and I hope I continue to make you proud.

Firefighters worked quickly to get the garage fire under control. However, fire entered the attic and spread quickly throughout the entire roofline. By 6:10 pm, fire officials reported the 13,000 square foot home was fully involved and firefighters were starting a defensive attack to contain the fire. Damages are extensive. No injuries were reported but HCEMS was on the scene checking firefighters for potential heat exhaustion. The cause of the fire will be under investigation by the Hamilton County Sheriffs Office. Family will be staying with neighbors.
